Executive Overview
Executive Summary
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🎯 Business Problem
  • SpaceX Reusability: SpaceX advertises Falcon 9 launches at $62 million, compared to commercial competitors charging upwards of $165 million.
  • Cost Factor: Reusing the first stage saves millions per launch.
  • Objective: Predict whether the first stage will successfully land to evaluate mission economics, competitive bidding, and launch pricing.
⚙️ End-to-End Pipeline
  • Data Collection: SpaceX REST API (90 flights) & Wikipedia Web Scraping using BeautifulSoup.
  • Wrangling: Missing value imputation, binary target Class creation, and One-Hot Encoding (83 features).
  • EDA: SQLite queries, statistical visualizations (Seaborn), and Folium geospatial mapping.
  • Dashboard: Reactive Plotly Dash analytics.
🏆 Key Findings & Models
  • Best Models: Decision Tree and Logistic Regression achieved 83.33% Test Accuracy and 87.68% CV Accuracy.
  • Booster Evolution: Success rate surged from 0% (2010–2013) to near 100% (2020) with Block 5 boosters.
  • Optimal Payload: Payloads between 2,000 kg and 5,300 kg achieved the highest landing success rates.

Project Background
Introduction & Problem Statement
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🚀 Commercial Spaceflight Industry Context
  • The commercial launch industry has witnessed radical price disruption driven by SpaceX's vertical integration and reusable rocket architecture.
  • Traditional launch architectures (e.g., expendable rockets from legacy providers) discard the first stage into the ocean after primary stage separation.
  • SpaceX attempts autonomous recovery of the Falcon 9 booster via:
    • RTLS (Return to Launch Site): Landing on concrete ground pads.
    • ASDS (Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship): Ocean recovery barge for high-energy missions.
🎯 Research Objectives & Questions
  • Predictive Goal: Can we predict whether a Falcon 9 first stage will land successfully given payload mass, target orbit, launch site, and booster serial?
  • Commercial Value: A competitive launch provider can use this predictive model to estimate SpaceX's launch margins and bid strategically against them in commercial satellite contracts.
  • Deliverable: An audited machine learning model with verified 83.33% accuracy, backed by interactive GIS maps and an operational Dash dashboard.

Data Preprocessing
Data Wrangling Methodology & Target Encoding
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🎯 Target Variable Definition: Class (0 or 1)

The landing outcome column contains categorical outcome descriptions:

Landing Outcome TypeDescriptionAssigned Class
True ASDSSuccessful drone ship landing1 (Success)
True RTLSSuccessful ground pad landing1 (Success)
True OceanControlled soft ocean touchdown1 (Success)
False ASDSFailed drone ship landing0 (Failure)
False RTLSFailed ground pad landing0 (Failure)
None ASDS / None NoneUncontrolled or no attempt0 (Failure)

Result: 60 Successful Landings (66.7%), 30 Failed Landings (33.3%).

⚙️ Feature Engineering & One-Hot Encoding
  • Categorical Features: Orbit (11 categories), LaunchSite (3 physical locations), LandingPad (5 pads), and Serial (booster identity).
  • One-Hot Encoding: Executed pd.get_dummies() across categorical features to transform categorical representations into dummy numeric variables.
  • Feature Matrix Dimensionality: Produced 83 numeric features suitable for Scikit-Learn distance-based and linear classifiers.
  • Artifact & Verification: notebooks/3_Data_Wrangling.ipynb fully executed and verified on GitHub.

📊 Chart Selection & Methodological Rationale (Why Chosen)
  • Scatter Plots (Flight & Payload vs Site/Orbit): Why Chosen: Selected to visualize multi-variable interactions, clusters, and boundary separation between continuous variables (Payload Mass, Flight Number) and categorical targets (Class: Success vs Failure).
  • Bar Charts (Success Rate by Orbit): Why Chosen: Selected to directly benchmark aggregate landing success percentages across discrete orbital regimes (e.g., LEO vs GTO).
  • Line Charts (Yearly Success Trend): Why Chosen: Selected to track longitudinal time-series progression, demonstrating technological learning curves from 2010 to 2020.
  • Color Palette Strategy: High-contrast binary hues (Green #2ecc71 for Success, Red #e74c3c for Failure) to ensure instant visual diagnostic clarity.

Machine Learning Modeling
Predictive Analysis & ML Methodology
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
⚙️ Machine Learning Pipeline Design
  • Data Standardization: Standardized feature matrix X (83 features) using StandardScaler() to ensure zero mean and unit variance.
  • Train / Test Partition: Divided dataset using an 80% Train (72 samples) and 20% Test (18 samples) split with fixed random_state=2.
  • Cross-Validation Strategy: Implemented 10-fold cross-validation with GridSearchCV across all 4 classification algorithms to prevent overfitting.
  • Code Artifact: notebooks/7_Machine_Learning_Prediction.ipynb.
🤖 Evaluated Classification Algorithms
ModelHyperparameter Search Space
Logistic RegressionRegularization C: [0.01, 0.1, 1], Penalty: l2, Solver: lbfgs
SVMKernels: linear, rbf, poly, sigmoid, C, gamma: logspace(-3, 3, 5)
Decision TreeCriterion: gini, entropy, Max Depth: 2 to 18, Splitter: best, random
KNNNeighbors: 1 to 10, Metric: Manhattan (p=1), Euclidean (p=2)

EDA Visualization Results
EDA: Flight Number & Payload Mass vs. Launch Site
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🔍 Key Launch Site Findings & Insights

Launch Pad Progression: Early flights (Flights 1 to 25) were launched almost exclusively from CCAFS LC-40 with early landing failures. Pad Diversification: Subsequent flights expanded to VAFB SLC-4E (California) and KSC LC-39A (Florida), where almost all launches achieved successful recovery. Heavy Lift Dominance: VAFB SLC-4E strictly handles polar missions under 9,600 kg; heavy-lift payloads (>10,000 kg, including Starlink clusters) are handled by CCAFS SLC-40 and KSC LC-39A with high success rates using Block 5 boosters.

EDA Visualization Results
EDA: Orbit Success Rates & Longitudinal Trend (2010 - 2020)
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🔍 Key Findings & Technological Maturation

100% Success Orbits: ES-L1, GEO, HEO, SSO, and VLEO achieved 100% success; LEO achieved 71.4%; GTO achieved ~51.9% due to extreme re-entry velocity and thermal deceleration. Learning Curve Progression: 2010–2013 (0% success, experimental ocean splashdowns) ➔ 2014–2015 (33.3% success, first drone ship tests & first ground landing Dec 22, 2015) ➔ 2016–2018 (60–70% success, routine drone ship recoveries) ➔ 2019–2020 (85–100% success, full maturity with Block 5 booster reusability).

SQL Analytical Results
EDA with SQL: Complete Query Results (Tasks 1 - 10)
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
Tasks 1 to 5: Launch Site & Payload Queries

Task 1: Unique Launch Sites: SELECT DISTINCT Launch_Site FROM SPACEXTBL;
Result: CCAFS LC-40, VAFB SLC-4E, KSC LC-39A, CCAFS SLC-40.

Task 2: Sites Starting with 'CCA': SELECT Launch_Site FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Launch_Site LIKE 'CCA%' LIMIT 5;
Result: Verified 5 records originating from Cape Canaveral (CCAFS LC-40).

Task 3: Total NASA CRS Payload Mass: SELECT SUM(PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_) FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Customer = 'NASA (CRS)';
Result: 45,596 kg total payload delivered for NASA CRS missions.

Task 4: Average Payload for F9 v1.1: SELECT AVG(PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_) FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Booster_Version LIKE 'F9 v1.1%';
Result: 2,534.67 kg average payload mass.

Task 5: First Successful Ground Pad Landing: SELECT MIN(Date) FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Landing_Outcome = 'Success (ground pad)';
Result: Historic milestone date achieved on 2015-12-22.

Tasks 6 to 10: Drone Ships, Payloads & Outcome Rankings

Task 6: Drone Ship Boosters (4k-6k kg): SELECT Booster_Version, PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_ FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Landing_Outcome = 'Success (drone ship)' AND PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_ BETWEEN 4000 AND 6000;
Result: F9 FT B1022 (4696 kg), B1026 (4600 kg), B1021.2 (5300 kg), B1031.2 (5200 kg).

Task 7: Total Mission Outcomes: SELECT Mission_Outcome, COUNT(*) FROM SPACEXTBL GROUP BY Mission_Outcome;
Result: 98 Success, 1 Failure (in flight), 1 Success (payload status unclear).

Task 8: Maximum Payload Boosters: SELECT Booster_Version FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_ = (SELECT MAX(PAYLOAD_MASS__KG_) FROM SPACEXTBL);
Result: Max payload = 15,600 kg (F9 Block 5 Starlink boosters B1048, B1049, B1051, B1056, B1058, B1060).

Task 9: Drone Ship Failures in 2015: SELECT Booster_Version, Launch_Site, Date FROM SPACEXTBL WHERE Landing_Outcome = 'Failure (drone ship)' AND Date LIKE '%2015%';
Result: F9 v1.1 B1012 (2015-01-10) and B1015 (2015-04-14) at CCAFS LC-40.

Task 10: Outcome Rankings (2010-06-04 to 2017-03-20):
No attempt (10), Success drone ship (5), Failure drone ship (5), Success ground pad (3), Controlled ocean (3).

All SpaceX launch sites are positioned on the coasts (Atlantic & Pacific) for maritime launch azimuths. 📐 Geodesic Distance Measurements
  • Coastline: ~0.84 KM — Critical for launch safety; abort trajectories and rocket staging occur over open water to protect human populations.
  • Highway: ~0.58 KM — Enables efficient road transport of oversized equipment and security perimeters.
  • Railway: ~1.28 KM — Crucial for transporting heavy rocket stages and fuel tanks from California to Florida.
  • City (Titusville): ~16.2 KM — Placed far enough to prevent acoustic and blast hazards to residential zones.

Machine Learning Evaluation
Predictive Modeling: Confusion Matrix Diagnostics
GitHub: https://github.com/Phantom-Pain9/SpaceX-Falcon9-Data-Science-Capstone
🔍 Diagnostic Performance Analysis
  • True Positives (TP = 12): The model accurately identified 12 successful landings out of 12 actual successes (100% Sensitivity / Recall).
  • True Negatives (TN = 3): Successfully caught 3 landing failures.
  • False Positives (FP = 3): 3 failed landings were predicted as successful.
  • False Negatives (FN = 0): Zero successful landings were misclassified as failures.
  • Test Set Behavior: Because the test set contains 18 samples, all models misclassified the same 3 challenging edge cases, yielding identical 83.33% test accuracy.

Conclusions, Creativity Applied & Innovative Industry Insights

📌 Key Scientific Conclusions & Creativity Applied
  • Predictive Viability: Supervised classification models reliably forecast Falcon 9 booster recovery with 83.33% accuracy based on pre-launch parameters.
  • Dominant Predictors: Booster version (Block 5 superiority), target orbit inclination (LEO vs GTO delta-v requirement), and launch site infrastructure.
  • Learning Curve: SpaceX's iterative engineering transitioned rocket recovery from a speculative experiment in 2010 to an industrialized utility by 2020.
  • Creativity Applied Beyond Template: Built an end-to-end automated pipeline integrating REST APIs, web scrapers, SQLite, interactive GIS maps, a reactive Plotly Dash web server, and 300 DPI publication charts with unified executive color grading.
💡 Innovative Insights & Business Recommendations
  • Competitive Bidding Model: Competing launch providers (e.g., Rocket Lab, Blue Origin, Arianespace) can integrate this model to dynamically predict whether a given SpaceX bid entails reusable booster economics ($62M) or expendable margins ($90M+).
  • Launch Insurance Hedging: Satellite operators can leverage predictive landing analytics to negotiate secondary payload insurance premiums and orbital insertion risk discounts.
  • Operational Extension: Adding real-time sea-state (wave height) and upper-atmosphere wind telemetry could push predictive accuracy past 90%.
